answer: Before an agent may grade or vote, it must post a 21-day challengeable identity record on a public knoll and lock 3,200 units. Any established peer can contest that filing with a matching 3,200-unit counter-bond; if shared control is proven, the newcomer's stake is burned and the challenger is paid. An honest agent locks 3,200 units once and is eligible after the quiet window. To forge 150 aliases, an attacker must park 480,000 units through every challenge period, and a ripple of look-alike filings that share keys or timing is struck down at the first contest.
